title.narrative: Circular solutions to plastic pollution in the Philippines

description.narrative: 162. This project brings multiple socio-economic benefits, including, health benefits for the general population, social and economic empowerment of people working in related industries, empowerment of related personnel and even the general population through knowledge management and communication practices, as well as the promotion of gender equality. Health Benefits: This project helps to phase-out the non-environmentally acceptable products (NEAP) and encourage the production and use of alternative, more sustainable and multi-use F&B packaging materials. This would reduce human exposure to hazardous chemicals that is sometimes present in single-use plastics. This will benefit not just workers in the F&B related industries, but wider population as consumers generally. Social and Economic Empowerment: To a certain extent, this project will catalyse the upgrade of the F&B packaging industry. This would mean the introduction of new materials, new technologies, and new business solutions. Necessarily, such will not only bring new employment opportunities, but also involve the training of related personnel and preparation of them for the uptake. Knowledge Empowerment: Through a series of knowledge sharing and learning activities designed for awareness-raising, this project will bring knowledge empowerment to both professionals working on (or in collaboration with) this project and the wider public. A deeper appreciation for circular economy approaches to the management of plastic products would be gained, and greater awareness for the hazards of single-use plastics will be achieved. Promotion of Gender Equality: This project has built in the principle of gender mainstreaming when designing its activities. The gender analysis report and gender action plan are attached as Annexes H and H(a). A range of activities have the requirement and expectations to achieve gender parity in the selection or participation process, while others are aimed to understand the gender-disaggregated information and to promote female leadership.
Development of sustainable policy and creation of innovative resource-efficient systems towards circular economy of plastic in the food and beverage sector
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.
